added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs. baseline_suite (2669319dd, scratch/base-full) records 13/13 files complete, 93 passed, 10 failed, 1 skipped, its failure ids being scatter_equivalence[1], escape_level_certificates[mastu-fullPulse-s1-4-5-B] and the eight test_wide_wall_record_builds_below_capacity ids, each reproducing with the same EXIT=1 in base-full-logs/. after_suite (ac3ce1b1e, the reviewed worktree) records 95 passed, 12 failed, 0 skipped. The set difference is exactly the two ids above. The sweep_bounds id is not caused by the change: the base arm skipped this test (its 1 skipped) because scratch/base-full could not resolve the receipt reference, and when the same reference module is supplied the identical ValueError broadcasting (256,) against (258,) reproduces at base (base-reference-supplement.log) exactly as at head (head-reference-supplement.log), so it is a pre-existing reference-capacity mismatch the change merely made run. The scatter id is a pytest-timeout during a JAX compile: both arms fail with 'Failed: Timeout (>300.0s) from pytest-timeout' at jax/_src/compiler.py, the base arm on case [1] and the head arm on [0] and [1], and the isolated head recheck of [0] passes (scatter-isolated-head.log, 1 passed in 110.97s, EXIT=0).

findings.text: The artifacts head_gate headline reads '13/13 complete: 96 passed, 10 failed, 0 deselected' but the run's own after_suite per-file runs sum to 95 passed and 12 failed, and head-full-gate.log reports four failed files against the base arm's three. A metric quoted from a gate log must be that log's own summary so the record reconciles with the log it cites; a reader trusting this headline under-counts the head arm's failures by two.

This test is one of the two added failures at the reviewed head and is not caused by the node's change, but its failure mode is uninformative and its base arm is missing: the base arm skipped it because scratch/base-full could not resolve the receipt reference, and when the reference is supplied the identical 256-versus-258 shape mismatch reproduces at base (base-reference-supplement.log), so the two arms are not compared over the same test set and the mismatch surfaces as 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (256,) (258,)' at scripts/prototypes/contour_tree_sweep_profile/profile.py:176 rather than as an assertion.

test_swept_arc_sets_are_invariant_to_carrier_edge_order[0] is the second added failure and is a JAX compilation timeout under concurrent load, not a topology result: head-full-logs/test_contour_tree_scatter_equivalence.log records 'Failed: Timeout (>300.0s) from pytest-timeout' inside jax/_src/compiler.py, the isolated head recheck passes in 110.97s (scatter-isolated-head.log, EXIT=0), and no base arm ever ran [0] in isolation, so its exemption rests on the isolated head pass alone.

When field_evaluator is None the added boundary and clipped-corner vertices keep vertex_psi as NaN while vertex_valid stays True (lines 249-251 and 270-275), so the placeholder is presented as a valid flux to any caller that builds a tree from the mesh. nova/equilibrium/topology.py:2594 is unharmed because it computes its own vertex_flux at topology.py:3119, but vertex_psi is exactly the argument every other caller feeds to build_contour_tree, so an omitted evaluator yields NaN node values rather than a refusal.
